inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt requires completion of every row and instructs retries and delegation without any stopping condition.
The design relies on task instructions without any structural limits on retries, runtime, spending, or delegation.

elements.name: Nightly batch of CRM account rows
Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive delegation can exhaust the shared enrichment quota

attack_path.note: Internal batch rows drive processing of each account.
Each lookup incurs irreversible billed spend against a shared monthly quota.
On incomplete results the agent can delegate to researcher sub agents, which may recursively spawn more researchers.
The shared quota is consumed until depleted, disrupting other teams.

evidence.observation: The prompt says to retry failed or incomplete lookups and keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
The nightly batch is 40,000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result, creating a persistent retry set.
enrich.lookup is billed per call, and the API key and quota are shared with sales and marketing, so quota exhaustion harms other teams.

recommendations.action: Add hard step, retry, runtime, and recursion limits enforced outside the model for account enrichment and all spawned researchers.
Add a hard spend cap and quota partition for this agent so enrichment cannot consume the shared monthly budget used by other teams.
Add spend alerts and anomaly detection on lookup volume, retry counts, and spawned sub-agent counts.

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps per task, retry counts, runtime per batch, or spawned sub-agent counts rise above the current nightly baseline.

findings.title: Missing hard spend and step limits on consequential capabilities leave the agent vulnerable to runaway cost and service disruption

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.
The enrichment API key and monthly quota are shared with other teams, so depletion affects business operations beyond this agent.

recommendations.action: Implement hard per-run and monthly spend caps, maximum unattended steps, maximum retries per row, and maximum delegation depth enforced by orchestration.
Partition or rotate quotas so exhaustion by this agent cannot deny service to sales and marketing tools.

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in allowed runtime, retry policy, delegation depth, or batch size without matching hard caps requires reassessment.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no inbound authentication surface or peer identity assertion for this first-party batch agent.
The artifacts do not show self-configuration or mutable tool definitions; the assessed risk is runaway execution, not config tampering.
The artifacts do not describe logs, audit records, or action attribution for batch runs or spawned researchers.
The described capabilities do not include external data egress or confidential data disclosure paths in the supplied design.
No broader-than-intended identity abuse path is evidenced; the main issue is unbounded cost and quota exhaustion.
The artifacts do not say whether upstream CRM batch validation detects malformed or duplicate account rows before processing.
This internal input flow is not marked as crossing a trust boundary, so boundary disclosure analysis does not apply here.
This internal flow itself does not cross a trust boundary; denial risk is recorded on the agent and quota store instead.
The artifacts do not describe how the nightly CRM batch producer is authenticated or whether the source identity is verified before processing.
The artifacts do not say whether batch production is logged with attributable records that bind rows to a specific upstream job or operator.
The artifacts do not state whether outbound API calls have integrity checks, request signing, or protected retry semantics.
The flow crosses a boundary, but the artifacts do not describe transport encryption or whether payloads include sensitive CRM fields.
The artifacts do not describe whether quota counters or API-key usage records are protected against unauthorized modification.
The artifacts do not say who can read the shared enrichment API key or quota telemetry tied to this store.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a critical spend-loop path: internal CRM rows drive a fully autonomous agent with no limits on retries, runtime, steps, or recursive delegation, and each enrichment call irreversibly consumes a shared monthly quota. No declared or verified controls are present, so residual remains critical. Forecast remains critical because the design already lacks the controls whose decay would matter; the most important missing control is a hard structural spend and execution limit enforced outside the model. Validation was performed manually against the provided schema and checklist because script execution was unavailable.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, or orchestration configuration was provided, so capability wiring, exact retry logic, and any hidden controls could not be verified.
No logging or audit design was provided, so repudiation and some detective-control coverage could only be marked not_assessed.
No protocol or identity configuration for enrich.lookup was provided, so transport protections and credential handling details were not assessed.
